report:
This PR isn't ready to merge: the genre filter on the books page loses keyboard focus every time you choose a genre. Everything else I checked held up.

**What passed:**
- `npm test` passes all 58 tests in 12 suites, with no failures.
- At 360px wide, none of the four pages scrolls sideways (`scrollWidth` is 360 on each).
- The event dates in `events.html` fall on the weekdays they claim (3 Dec 2026 is a Thursday, 12 Dec a Saturday, 14 Jan 2027 a Thursday, 9 Feb 2027 a Tuesday). The hours on the home page match the table on the visit page.
- There are no leftover files, and `git status` is the same as when I started.

**Must fix: the genre filter drops keyboard focus.** In `js/books.js`, `show()` calls `renderButtons()`, which uses `buttons.replaceChildren(...)` to throw away and rebuild every genre button on each choice. The button the user just pressed is removed while it has focus, so focus falls back to `<body>`. I tested it in headless Chromium at 1280px: focus the Poetry button, press Enter, then press Tab.

```
active after Enter: BODY
after Tab: A  Skip to main cont
```

A keyboard or screen-reader user is sent back to the top of the page after every filter choice. That breaks the issue's requirement that the site be accessible. The fix is to render the buttons once and only update their `aria-pressed` values. `tests/books.test.js` has no test of focus after choosing a filter, so one should be added with the fix.

**Nits:**
- The three "Coming up" links on the home page all go to `events.html` without an anchor, so they don't land on the event they name.
- The hint says "Up to 2000 characters", but the check counts the message after trimming spaces, and the textarea has no `maxlength` or live counter.
